bull.b: Higher earnings, ROTCE and operating leverage indicate that revenue growth is translating into stronger capital efficiency. If expense discipline and management’s medium-term initiatives persist, profitability can improve beyond the current reporting period.

bull.t: Diversified fee businesses and private-bank growth
bull.b: Expansion in capital markets, wealth management and the Private Bank broadens Citizens’ revenue mix beyond spread income. These relationship-based businesses can deepen customer ties, support deposit gathering and provide recurring fee growth over time.

bull.t: Broad loan growth and improving credit quality
bull.b: Loan growth across commercial, retail and private-bank businesses supports future interest income, while lower charge-offs and non-accruals suggest resilient underwriting and portfolio quality. This combination strengthens the bank’s ability to grow without a proportionate rise in credit costs.

bear.t: Weakening cash-flow momentum and higher leverage
bear.b: Although cash generation remains positive, the year-over-year decline and higher leverage reduce financial flexibility. Sustained pressure could constrain balance-sheet growth, increase reliance on external funding or make it harder to absorb unexpected credit and capital demands.

bear.t: Deposit-cost pressure and temporary wholesale funding
bear.b: Rising deposit costs can compress net interest margins, particularly when loan pricing cannot adjust as quickly. Increased FHLB usage also shows that funding growth temporarily outpaced deposits, creating an ongoing need to manage liquidity and funding mix carefully.

bear.t: Capital flexibility constrained by CET1 and preferred-stock terms
bear.b: CET1 modestly below the internal reference point leaves less room for aggressive balance-sheet expansion or shareholder returns. The new preferred-stock terms add constraints across the equity stack, making capital allocation and distribution planning more complex.
